# Incident note: Sustained casing annulus pressure on W-12

**Document ID:** IN-066
**Event ID:** EV-0179
**Note date:** 2026-10-28
**Well:** W-12 (Field A, vertical, natural flow)
**Severity:** High
**Status at note date:** Open
**Prepared by:** Production Engineer

## What happened
On 2026-10-28 the B-annulus pressure on W-12 rose above the allowed limit and did not bleed off. The pressure returned after each bleed-down attempt, which is consistent with sustained casing pressure rather than thermal build-up. The well was shut in pending integrity diagnostics.

## Immediate actions
- Well shut in and the wellhead area checked for visible leaks, with none reported.
- Annulus pressure readings logged at regular intervals after shut-in.
- Production Supervisor and Integrity Engineer informed.
- Access to the wellhead restricted to essential checks only.

## Findings so far
- The annulus pressure did not bleed off to the expected level.
- No cause has been confirmed. Possible sources, such as a tubing or packer leak or a casing issue, are not yet ruled in or out.
- Diagnostics are not yet complete.

## Impact
- Downtime as of this note: 24 hours.
- Production before the event (7 days to 2026-10-27): oil 650.7 bbl/d, gas 306.6 Mscf/d, water cut 21.8 %, GOR 471 scf/bbl.
- Production on 2026-10-28: oil 0 bbl, gas 0 Mscf, uptime 0 hours.
- Deferred oil is running at about the pre-event rate of 650.7 bbl/d for as long as the well stays shut in.

## Status at note date
Open. W-12 remains shut in. No restart is planned until the diagnostics are reviewed and the well is confirmed to be within its barrier limits.

## Next actions
1. Run the annulus bleed-down and build-up test per the procedure and record the results.
2. Review the results with the Integrity Engineer to identify the likely leak path.
3. Decide on further diagnostics or an intervention plan.
4. Update the deferred production estimate daily.
5. Keep this note open until the well is cleared or repaired.

## Applicable procedure
SOP-INT-010 Well Integrity: Annulus Pressure Management

# Incident note: Flowline leak on W-36

**Document ID:** IN-069
**Event ID:** EV-0183
**Note date:** 2026-11-18
**Well:** W-36 (Bayda, horizontal, natural flow)
**Severity:** High
**Status at note date:** Open
**Applicable procedure:** SOP-HSE-006 Flowline Leak Response

## What happened
During a routine patrol on 2026-11-18, the Lead Operator found a pinhole leak on the W-36 flowline near the manifold. The leak was a small, steady weep with no spray.

## Immediate actions
- W-36 was shut in.
- The affected section was isolated and depressurised.
- The area was barricaded and signed, and the HSE Advisor was informed.
- Spill containment was placed under the leak point and the small volume of released fluid was cleaned up.

## Findings so far
- The leak is at a single pinhole on the flowline pipe body close to the manifold tie-in.
- The cause is not yet confirmed. The Integrity Engineer will review external and internal corrosion and erosion as possible contributors, given the sand-prone nature of Bayda.
- No related events on this well in the last 30 days.

## Impact
- Downtime as of the note date: 24 hours.
- Production on 2026-11-18: 0 bbl oil, 0 Mscf gas, uptime 0 hours.
- The 7-day average before the event (ending 2026-11-17) was 1832.5 bbl/d oil, 2506.7 Mscf/d gas, 13.1 % water cut and GOR 1368 scf/bbl. Deferred oil is therefore building at roughly that oil rate each day while the well stays shut in.

## Status
Open. The well remains shut in and the area stays isolated. A clamp repair is pending.

## Next actions
1. Maintenance Planner to schedule the clamp repair and raise the work order.
2. Integrity Engineer to perform thickness checks on the flowline around the leak and along the adjacent sections.
3. HSE Advisor to confirm the permit to work and gas testing requirements before the repair starts.
4. Following the repair, carry out a pressure test and a leak check before restart.
5. Production Engineer to plan a controlled restart and a follow-up well test to confirm rates against the baseline.

Response steps follow SOP-HSE-006 Flowline Leak Response. This note will be updated when the repair is completed and the incident is closed.

# Incident note: Sand production alarm on W-34

**Document id:** IN-067
**Event id:** EV-0180
**Note date:** 2026-11-09
**Well:** W-34 (Bayda, horizontal, gas lift)
**Severity:** High
**Status at note date:** Open

## What happened
On 2026-11-09 the acoustic sand monitor on W-34 alarmed above threshold. The erosion probe on the flowline shows metal loss. The well is still producing.

## Immediate actions
- Choke reduced again to 24/64.
- Sand sampling set to every shift.
- Lead Operator informed the Production Supervisor and the CPF-1 control room.
- Flowline walk-down carried out at surface; no leak or visible damage found.

## Findings so far
- The alarm and the probe metal loss point to active sand production from the well.
- Water cut on the day was 32.8%, against 30.7% in the 7 days before the event (to 2026-11-08).
- No related events on this well in the last 30 days.
- The cause is not yet confirmed. Investigation is open.

## Impact
| Item | Before (7 days to 2026-11-08) | On 2026-11-09 |
|---|---|---|
| Oil | 723 bbl/d | 493.3 bbl |
| Gas | 1380.6 Mscf/d | 837.3 Mscf |
| Water cut | 30.7% | 32.8% |
| Uptime | n/a | 22 h |

Downtime as of the note date is 2 hours. The pre-event GOR was 1910 scf/bbl. Oil on the day was about 230 bbl below the previous 7-day average, mostly from the choke reduction and the 2 hours of downtime.

## Status at note date
Open. The well is producing on the 24/64 choke under increased monitoring.

## Next actions
1. Continue sand sampling every shift and record the results against the alarm threshold.
2. Production Engineer to review the sand trend and the erosion probe readings.
3. Integrity Engineer to assess flowline wall loss and schedule thickness checks.
4. Hold the choke at 24/64 until the investigation gives direction.
5. Follow the alarm response steps in SOP-OPS-002 Sand Management and Sand Production Alarms.

**Author:** Production Engineer

# Incident note: Wellhead pressure anomaly on W-05

**Document ID:** IN-068
**Note date:** 2026-11-15
**Event ID:** EV-0181
**Well:** W-05 (Field A, vertical, ESP)
**Severity:** medium
**Status at note date:** open

## What happened
On 2026-11-15 the flowing wellhead pressure on W-05 began swinging by plus or minus 60 psi with no choke change. The well remains on production.

## Immediate actions
- The Lead Operator confirmed the choke position had not been changed.
- The wellhead gauge was checked against a reference gauge and read correctly, so an instrument fault is considered unlikely.
- The Production Supervisor was informed.
- The well was kept online under closer monitoring, with pressure readings taken at shorter intervals.

## Findings so far
The working suspicion is partial plugging of the choke. This is not confirmed. No ESP trip or alarm was reported in connection with the swings.

## Impact
- Downtime as of the note date: 3 hours (uptime on the day 21 hours).
- Production on 2026-11-15: oil 685.6 bbl, gas 631.5 Mscf, water cut 28.5%.
- Baseline for the 7 days to 2026-11-14: oil 784.3 bbl/d, gas 700.4 Mscf/d, water cut 29.7%, GOR 893 scf/bbl.
- Oil on the day was about 98.7 bbl below the baseline daily rate, consistent with the lost hours and the unstable flow. Water cut is essentially unchanged, so a change in reservoir fluid is not indicated at this point.

## Status
Open. The well is producing and under monitoring. No related events were recorded in the last 30 days. No specific procedure applies to this event.

## Next actions
1. The Production Engineer will review the pressure trend over the next shifts to see whether the swings persist or grow.
2. If the swings continue, plan a choke inspection or change-out, with the downtime scheduled to limit deferred oil.
3. Check ESP motor current and intake data for any sign of a downhole cause.
4. Update this note once the cause is confirmed or the swings stop.

**Prepared by:** Production Engineer

# Incident note: ESP high vibration on W-25

**Document ID:** IN-070
**Note date:** 2026-11-20
**Event ID:** EV-0184
**Well:** W-25 (Field B, deviated, ESP)
**Severity:** medium
**Status at note date:** open
**Prepared by:** Production Engineer

## What happened
On 2026-11-20 the downhole sensor on W-25 showed ESP vibration rising above the alarm level. The well stayed on line, but the unit was brought down for a short period and the frequency was then reduced from 55 to 50 Hz.

## Immediate actions
- The Lead Operator confirmed the alarm on the controller and the surface readings.
- Drive frequency reduced from 55 to 50 Hz and the response was watched.
- The Production Supervisor was informed.
- Vibration, motor current and intake pressure trends are now logged at a higher frequency.

## Findings so far
The vibration trend is still under review. No root cause is confirmed. The cause is not yet known, and the trend after the frequency reduction needs more hours of data before conclusions are drawn.

## Impact
- Downtime as of this note: 2 hours.
- Uptime on the day: 22 hours.
- Production on 2026-11-20: 327.5 bbl oil, 268.4 Mscf gas, water cut 41.5%.
- Baseline for the 7 days to 2026-11-19: 407.7 bbl/d oil, 333 Mscf/d gas, water cut 39%, GOR 817 scf/bbl.
- Oil on the day was about 80 bbl below the baseline rate, partly from the 2 hours of downtime and partly from the lower frequency.

## Status
Open. The well is producing at 50 Hz under close watch. No related events were recorded on this well in the last 30 days.

## Next actions
1. Review the vibration trend over the next shifts at 50 Hz.
2. Compare the vibration signature with earlier data from this pump.
3. Hold the frequency at 50 Hz until the Production Engineer approves a change.
4. Escalate to the ESP vendor if vibration rises again or stays above the alarm level.
5. Update this note when the trend is understood.

## Procedure reference
SOP-OPS-001 ESP Trip Response and Restart applies. Follow it for any trip, and do not restart after a vibration trip until the engineer has reviewed the data.

answer.answer: Five incidents are open: W-12 and W-05 in Field A, W-25 in Field B, and W-36 and W-34 in Bayda. High severity: W-12 is shut in over annulus pressure that won't bleed off [1]; W-36 is shut in for a flowline leak awaiting a clamp repair [2]; W-34 has a sand alarm and a reduced choke [3]. Medium severity: W-05 has pressure swings [4] and W-25 has high pump vibration [5].
answer.could_not_verify: Root causes are unconfirmed in all five notes.
